job.title: Executive Director, Finance
job.description:
Connected People is proud to be partnering with the Catholic Diocese of Maitland-Newcastle to appoint an experienced and accomplished Executive Director, Finance.

The Diocese is a highly regarded organisation with a longstanding commitment to serving communities throughout the Newcastle, Hunter and Manning regions.

Through its extensive network of Catholic Schools, CatholicCare, St Nicholas Early Education, Catholic Community Fund, , parishes and shared services, the Diocese delivers essential educational, social welfare, pastoral and community services.

Employing approximately 5,500 people across more than 100 locations, with consolidated annual revenue of approximately $640 million and $1.6 billion in assets under management, the Diocese operates within a diverse and sophisticated financial and governance environment.

The Opportunity
Reporting directly to the Managing Director and serving as a key member of the Diocesan Leadership Group, the Executive Director, Finance will provide strategic financial leadership, oversight and direction across the Diocese and its agencies.

This is an influential executive appointment, responsible for ensuring the long-term financial sustainability of the organisation while supporting its strategic priorities and operational objectives.

As a trusted adviser to the Bishop, Managing Director, Trustees and senior leadership, you will provide strategic financial advice, strengthen financial governance and support informed decision-making across a complex, multi-entity organisation.

Leading a multidisciplinary finance team encompassing accounting, finance business partnering, payroll, procurement, financial systems and project management, you will oversee financial strategy, planning, reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cash flow management, regulatory compliance and audit.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and implement financial strategies supporting long-term sustainability, organisational priorities and effective resource allocation.
  • Provide strategic financial advice to the Managing Director, Bishop, Trustees and Diocesan Leadership Group.
  • Oversee financial reporting, budgeting, forecasting, cashflow management and capital expenditure planning across the Diocese and its agencies.
  • Lead and develop a high-performing finance team, fostering a culture of collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Strengthen financial governance, internal controls, risk management and regulatory compliance.
  • Drive improvements in financial systems, policies, processes and reporting capability to support operational effectiveness and strategic decision-making.

About You
We are seeking an accomplished finance executive who combines strong technical expertise and commercial acumen with exceptional leadership capability and a genuine commitment to organisational purpose.

You will be a collaborative and values-driven leader, comfortable navigating sophisticated financial environments and building trusted relationships with executive stakeholders, governing bodies and operational leaders.
The successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • CA qualifications, together with postgraduate qualifications or equivalent senior financial leadership experience.
  • A minimum of five years' experience in a similar senior finance leadership position, with proven executive leadership capability.
  • Extensive experience in financial strategy, governance, reporting, budgeting and risk management within a complex organisation.
  • Demonstrated success leading multidisciplinary finance teams and driving organisational improvement.
  • Strong analytical capability and the ability to translate complex financial information into clear, commercially informed strategic advice.
  • Excellent communication, influencing and stakeholder engagement skills, including experience working with executive leadership teams and governing boards.
  • A considered, ethical and collaborative leadership style.

Experience within large education, not-for-profit, community services, or similarly complex multi-entity environments will be highly regarded.

In accordance with the position requirements, applicants will be required to be Catholic. A commitment to upholding the ethos, mission and values of the Catholic Diocese is essential.

What's on Offer
This is an exceptional opportunity to join a respected, purpose-driven organisation where your leadership will contribute to meaningful outcomes across the community.

The Diocese offers an attractive executive package, including:

  • Competitive remuneration of $300,000–$320,000 plus superannuation.
  • Dedicated Executive Assistant support.
  • Free on-site parking at the Newcastle office.
  • Opportunities for continued professional development and career growth.
  • Relocation assistance available for candidates considering a move to the Newcastle region.

Beyond the remuneration and benefits, this appointment provides an opportunity to influence the financial direction of an organisation that plays an important role in the lives of thousands of people.

Connected People has been engaged to manage this executive appointment. We welcome confidential conversations with suitably qualified executives interested in exploring the opportunity.

For further information, please contact Monica Walmsley, Director of Connected People, on 0492 300 464, or email monica@connectedpeople.com.au.

Alternatively, please apply through SEEK.

All enquiries will be treated with the strictest confidence.

job.title: Practice Manager | Legal Operations
job.description:
Connected People is proud to be partnering with one of NSW's leading law firms to recruit a Practice Manager based in their Sydney CBD office.

This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced legal operations professional to join a growing and highly regarded firm, taking ownership of day-to-day practice operations, workflow management and team performance across its Sydney and Newcastle offices.

Unlike many traditional Practice Manager positions, this role is focused purely on legal operations and people leadership, without responsibility for HR, finance or accounts.

About the Firm:

 Our client is a highly respected and established law firm with offices in Sydney and Newcastle. The firm has built an excellent reputation for delivering high-quality legal services while maintaining a supportive, collaborative and people-focused culture.

Continued growth has created the need for a dedicated Practice Manager who can support the firm's people, improve operational efficiencies and ensure teams have the resources and processes needed to perform at their best.

With strong staff retention and a dynamic leadership team, this is an opportunity to join a firm that genuinely values its people and is committed to continued growth and improvement.

About the Role:

Reporting directly to a senior member of the firm's leadership team, you will take responsibility for overseeing the day-to-day operations of the firm's legal teams, ensuring workloads, resources and processes are managed effectively.

You'll play a pivotal role in identifying opportunities for improvement, implementing operational changes and supporting team members through periods of growth and change.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Oversee day-to-day legal practice operations across the Sydney and Newcastle offices.
  • Manage workflows, resource allocation, workloads and staffing requirements to ensure efficient service delivery.
  • Provide hands-on people leadership, supporting team performance, engagement and satisfaction.
  • Identify and implement operational improvements that enhance productivity, efficiency and profitability.
  • Lead and support change management initiatives, ensuring teams are engaged and supported throughout the process.
  • Work closely with the leadership team to understand commercial priorities and translate these into practical operational improvements.
  • Balance competing priorities and respond proactively to the evolving needs of a busy legal practice.
  • Foster a positive, collaborative and high-performing team environment.

The position will be based in Sydney CBD, with travel to the Newcastle office approximately one day per fortnight. All travel expenses will be covered by the firm.

About You:
 We're looking for a commercially minded and resilient Practice Manager who combines strong operational experience with a genuine passion for leading people.

Ideally, you'll have experience working within a medium to large law firm (50+ employees), where you've developed an understanding of the complexities of managing workloads, resources and competing priorities.

Experience in defendant insurance, personal injury or a fixed-fee legal environment would be highly regarded, although it is not essential.

You'll also bring:

  • Demonstrated experience in legal practice management, legal operations or a similar leadership role.
  • Strong workflow and resource management capabilities.
  • Proven ability to lead teams, manage change and drive operational improvements.
  • Commercial acumen and an understanding of how operational efficiencies contribute to business performance.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence and the ability to build trusted relationships.
  • A resilient, adaptable and solutions-focused approach.
  • The ability to manage competing demands while maintaining a positive and supportive team environment.

Above all, we're looking for someone who can see the bigger picture, understand the reasons behind change and bring people along on the journey.

What's on Offer?

  • Competitive salary package, commensurate with experience.
  • A newly created leadership opportunity with genuine scope to make an impact.
  • Sydney CBD location.
  • A supportive, collaborative and highly regarded law firm.
  • The opportunity to work closely with an experienced and commercially focused leadership team.
  • Hybrid working arrangements available following a successful six-month probation period.
  • Fully funded travel to the Newcastle office.
  • Ongoing professional development and career opportunities.
  • A positive workplace culture with a genuine focus on employee wellbeing and satisfaction.

If you're an experienced legal professional who enjoys leading people, improving processes and making a meaningful contribution to a firm's success, we'd love to hear from you.

For a confidential discussion, please contact Monica Walmsley at Connected People on 0492 300 464, or apply now.

At Connected People, we specialise in legal recruitment and take a personalised approach to helping candidates find opportunities that align with their experience, values and career aspirations. If this role isn't quite right for you, we'd still welcome a confidential conversation about your next career move.

All enquiries will be treated with the strictest confidence.

job.title: Finance Officer
job.description:
Opportunity to join one of Newcastle’s longest‑established law firms, known for their commitment to excellence, integrity, and client service. They are seeking a highly organised, detail‑driven Finance Officer to join the team in a full‑time capacity on site.

About the Role
As the Finance Officer, you will be responsible for the smooth operation of the firm’s financial, trust, payroll, and reporting functions. Working closely with the General Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring accuracy, compliance, and efficiency across all financial processes.

This is a hands‑on role with a strong focus on daily accounting tasks, trust account compliance, payroll processing, and monthly reporting.

Key Responsibilities

Accounting

  • Enter creditor invoices into Xero daily
  • Process EFT and direct credit payments
  • Reconcile XERO receivables/payables with CBA activity
  • Manage accounts payable and credit card reconciliations
  • Run monthly XERO reports including P&L and Trial Balance
  • Monitor lease, licence, and subscription payments
  • Manage petty cash and internal company loan records
  • Process IAS, PAYG, BAS when required

Trust Account Compliance (this can be taught)

  • Review daily trust account movements
  • Verify instructions and authorities with the GM
  • Run end‑of‑month trust reconciliations and reports
  • Assist with annual trust audit requirements

Payroll

  • Prepare and reconcile fortnightly payroll
  • Enter payroll into XERO and submit to ATO
  • Process superannuation, payroll tax, deductions, and final payments
  • Load payroll for payment via CBA

Reporting & Office Support

  • Prepare monthly and quarterly reports
  • Maintain financial records (hard copy & SharePoint)
  • Manage kitchen supplies and supermarket account
  • Support the General Manager and broader team as required

About You
You will bring a strong eye for detail, excellent organisational skills, and the ability to work independently while supporting a busy legal practice.

Desired Skills

  • A number of years in a similar role, ideally in a professional services type business
  • Accounting qualifications highly regarded, Cert IV etc
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills
  • High accuracy and attention to detail
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, Outlook
  • Ability to work with repetitive tasks while maintaining accuracy
  • Ideally solid experiences with Xero
  • Someone looking for a long term role rather than a stepping stone role
  • Happy to work full time in the office during normal business hours

job.title: Associate/Senior Associate | Construction Disputes
job.description:
If you’re a commercial or civil litigator who enjoys complex disputes but would like to develop a genuine specialisation, this is an opportunity worth exploring.

Our client is an established commercial law firm with a highly regarded construction practice and a strong, long-term client base across the commercial, industrial, education, health, hospitality, residential and infrastructure sectors.

Due to continued growth, the team is looking for an Associate or Senior Associate to join its construction disputes practice.

The Opportunity
Working closely with an experienced Partner in a small, hands-on construction team, you’ll have the opportunity to develop genuine expertise across the full construction project lifecycle.

Your work will include:

  • Construction and commercial disputes
  • Court proceedings and litigation
  • Security of Payment matters
  • Contractual disputes and risk management
  • Advice arising during project delivery
  • Post-completion disputes
  • Exposure to front-end construction matters as the practice continues to grow
  • Direct interaction with clients and opportunities to attend client sites


The firm acts for a diverse range of construction industry participants, including developers, builders, contractors, consultants, architects, engineers, manufacturers, trades and subcontractors.

Importantly, you don’t need to already be a construction specialist. This could be an excellent move for a capable commercial or civil litigator who wants to build a long-term career in construction law.

Why Consider This Role?
Become a genuine specialist
You’ll work alongside experienced construction lawyers who are invested in developing your technical capability, with exposure to interesting disputes and the commercial realities sitting behind them.

Real client exposure
This isn’t a role where you’ll spend your career several layers removed from the client. You’ll gain exposure to a strong repeat-client base, learn where instructions come from and develop meaningful commercial relationships.

A firm that takes development seriously
There is a genuine focus on training and broader professional development, including leadership programs featuring speakers from business and other industries. Lawyers are also encouraged to understand their clients’ businesses and the technical issues behind construction projects, not simply the law.

Career development without a one-size-fits-all pathway
Not everyone wants to become a Partner, and that’s understood here. If your goal is instead to become an exceptional technical lawyer, that pathway will be supported too.

A grown-up culture
The firm has a hardworking team that takes pride in the quality of its work, while recognising that work isn’t everything. There is a collaborative approach to learning, a good gender mix across levels and a professional but down-to-earth environment.

What We’re Looking For

  • A genuine interest in specialising in construction disputes
  • Confidence dealing directly with clients and taking increasing ownership of matters
  • 3+ years’ PAE
  • Commercial litigation, civil litigation and/or construction disputes experience
  • Strong drafting, analytical and technical skills
  • Exposure to running or assisting with court proceedings
  • Security of Payment experience would be advantageous, but isn’t essential


The Package & Environment

  • Competitive market salary
  • Bonus structure
  • Full-time permanent position
  • Sydney CBD location, close to Wynyard
  • Modern office fit-out
  • Flexibility to work from home as needed
  • Established administrative and paralegal support
  • Strong emphasis on technical training, mentorship and career development


Interested?

For a confidential discussion, contact Elizabeth at Connected People on 0455 326 852 for a chat, or apply directly for further information.

All enquiries will be treated in strict confidence.

What's on Offer?
